Bar graphs turn counting into pictures. Let's learn to read them!

🎯 What you'll learn here

In this part of the map, you'll learn to read a bar graph, find the tallest and shortest bars, and figure out what the numbers mean.

Learning Outcome

  • Read a bar graph
  • Compare bars (tallest, shortest, same)
  • Answer questions using graph data
Bar Graphs

What is it?

A bar graph is a graphical representation of data — a common statistical tool used for organizing information so it's easier to compare and analyze.

Parts of a Bar Graph

Title➡What it's about
Axis➡The number scale
Bars➡Height = the amount

📊 What is a bar graph?

A bar graph uses rectangles (bars) to compare the size of different groups. The taller the bar, the bigger the number. Bar graphs can stand up (vertical) or lie down (horizontal).

✍️ Write this definition in your notebook

A bar graph shows: Apples 5, Bananas 8, Grapes 3. Which fruit is the class's favorite, and which is the least favorite?

🖐️ Active strategy: Find the tallest and shortest bars first.

Bananas (tallest bar) is the favorite; Grapes (shortest bar) is the least favorite

✍️ Make your own bar graph of your classmates' favorite fruit.
